denial.label: Pre-existing disease waiting period not completed

grounds: Osteoarthritis of knee was first diagnosed on 2026-03-21, AFTER the policy start date 2024-08-07; by definition it is not a Pre-Existing Disease, so the waiting period does not apply.
letter:
Subject: Appeal against Denial D03 – Pre‑Existing Disease Waiting Period – Claim ID c43f8bac-9113-4e45-aece-6c8b88e416b5  

Claim Details:  
- Claim ID: c43f8bac-9113-4e45-aece-6c8b88e416b5  
- Patient ID: 78be6008-8ddb-4c52-8b84-2f5f6b25aff6  
- Patient Name: Gopal Naidu  
- Date of Claim Creation: 27‑04‑2026  
- Policy: Suraksha Gold Family Floater Plan (Plan Code SGH‑GOLD) – Coverage Start 07‑08‑2024  
- Diagnosis: Osteoarthritis of knee (onset 21‑03‑2026)  
- Procedure: Physical therapy procedure (orthopedic category)  
- Claim Amount: INR 48,639.08  

Grounds for Appeal:  
The diagnosis of osteoarthritis of the knee was first made on 21‑03‑2026, which is after the policy start date of 07‑08‑2024. According to the definition of Pre‑Existing Disease, a condition first diagnosed on or after the policy start date is not a Pre‑Existing Disease and therefore is not subject to the 24‑month waiting period [suraksha_gold_policy#5]. The insurer’s denial relies on the pre‑existing disease waiting period, but that clause applies only to conditions meeting the definition in Clause 2.2, which is not satisfied in this case [suraksha_gold_policy#10].  

Burden of Proof:  
Under the claims procedure, the insurer bears the burden of proving that an exclusion or waiting period applies and must provide documentary evidence of a diagnosis prior to the policy start date. No such evidence has been presented. The insurer therefore has not met its evidentiary obligation [claims_procedure_and_grievance#6].  

Clinical Necessity:  
Physical therapy for osteoarthritis of the knee is a medically necessary treatment as defined by the policy (treatment required for the medical management of the illness and prescribed by a medical practitioner) [suraksha_gold_policy#4]. The treating orthopaedic specialist will attach clinical notes confirming the necessity of the prescribed physical therapy.  

Reference to Denial Standards and Appeal Rights:  
The insured (or provider) has the right to appeal a denial in writing within 30 days of the denial letter, identifying the claim, denial reason, policy clauses, and supporting clinical evidence [claims_procedure_and_grievance#8]. The insurer’s grievance cell must acknowledge the appeal within 3 working days and decide within 15 days; if the denial is overturned, payment must be made with interest for the period of delay [claims_procedure_and_grievance#9].  

Specific Request:  
In view of the above, we request that the denial be rescinded, the claim be re‑processed, and the amount of INR 48,639.08 be paid without further delay, together with any interest accrued due to the period of non‑payment as mandated by the grievance timelines.  

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.  

Insurance Desk (on behalf of the treating provider)

citations.section: Suraksha Gold Family Floater Plan (Policy Wording) > 4. Waiting Periods > 4.2 Pre-Existing Disease Waiting Period
citations.quote:
### 4.2 Pre-Existing Disease Waiting Period
Expenses related to a Pre-Existing Disease (Clause 2.2) are covered after 24 months of continuous coverage from the first policy start date. This waiting period applies ONLY to conditions meeting the definition in Clause 2.2.

citations.section: Suraksha Gold Family Floater Plan (Policy Wording) > 2. Definitions > 2.2 Pre-Existing Disease (PED)
citations.quote:
### 2.2 Pre-Existing Disease (PED)
Pre-Existing Disease means any condition diagnosed by a physician, or for which medical advice or treatment was received, within 48 months PRIOR TO the first policy start date. citations.section: Claims Procedure, Denial Standards and Grievance Redressal > C3. Standards for Denial > C3.2 Burden of Proof for Exclusions and Waiting Periods
citations.quote:
### C3.2 Burden of Proof for Exclusions and Waiting Periods
The insurer bears the burden of proving that an exclusion or waiting period applies. For a Pre-Existing Disease denial, the insurer must show documentary evidence that the condition was diagnosed or treated before the policy start date.

citations.section: Claims Procedure, Denial Standards and Grievance Redressal > C4. Appeals and Grievances > C4.2 Timelines
citations.quote:
### C4.2 Timelines
The insurer's grievance cell must acknowledge an appeal within 3 working days and decide it within 15 days. If the denial is overturned, the claim must be paid with interest for the period of delay.

citations.section: Suraksha Gold Family Floater Plan (Policy Wording) > 2. Definitions > 2.1 Medically Necessary
citations.quote:
## 2. Definitions  
### 2.1 Medically Necessary
Treatment required for the medical management of the illness or injury, not exceeding the level of care necessary for safe, adequate and appropriate care, and prescribed by a medical practitioner in line with generally accepted standards of practice.

citations.section: Claims Procedure, Denial Standards and Grievance Redressal > C4. Appeals and Grievances > C4.1 Right to Appeal
citations.quote:
## C4. Appeals and Grievances  
### C4.1 Right to Appeal
The insured, or the provider on the insured's behalf, may appeal a denial in writing within 30 days of the denial letter. The appeal should identify the claim, the denial reason, the policy clauses relied upon and the supporting clinical evidence.
